##### Project general facts

DAMAC Tower Nine Elms is a residential tower designed by the architectural firm Kohn Pedersen Fox. The building combines light-coloured stone, glass, ceramic panels and warm terracotta in a staggered form, and offers studio, one, two and three bedroom apartments along with a small collection of duplex penthouse suites. Every home opens onto a glazed winter garden with wide views across the city.

Residents enjoy an indoor swimming pool, a Jacuzzi and a sun deck, a fully equipped gym, a private cinema, a residents' lounge and a dedicated children's play area, all set on high floors with panoramic city views. Landscaped roof gardens and terraces provide outdoor space above the streets, while a double-height entrance lobby and a round-the-clock concierge complete the service.

Interiors feature wood flooring in the living areas, stone flooring in the hallways and fitted wardrobes in the bedrooms. Kitchens come with lacquered cabinetry, composite stone worktops and integrated appliances, and bathrooms are finished in marble or ceramic tiles with heated towel rails. Apartments are delivered with thermostatically controlled heating and cooling.

##### Parking

Valet parking.

##### Location description and benefits

Nine Elms is a regenerated riverside district on the south bank of the River Thames, set between Vauxhall and Battersea in central London. The area is served by Vauxhall station and by the Nine Elms and Battersea Power Station stations on the Northern Line, giving quick access to the West End, the City and Gatwick Airport by rail.

The neighbourhood is home to the landmark Battersea Power Station, the New Covent Garden Market and the United States Embassy, along with a riverside frontage with cafés and public spaces. Battersea Park offers green space, sports courts and a children's zoo, while Chelsea, Knightsbridge, Sloane Square and Kensington are within easy reach for shopping, dining and culture.

A large-scale regeneration programme has transformed Nine Elms into a modern residential quarter and an internationally significant business district. Its transport links, riverside setting and proximity to central London make the district a popular choice for both owner-occupiers and investors.
